title: Embedding model onboarding, versioning, and automated rollout/deprecation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Define and implement a reproducible onboarding flow for new embedding models (open and curated), a deterministic versioning scheme, and an automated rollout + deprecation pipeline tied to telemetry and quality gates. Goal is to reduce manual work for model owners, avoid accidental breaking changes for customers, and ensure safe, measurable rollouts that respect latency and quality SLOs.

Background: We frequently add new embedding models and vector variants (quantized / float) to the model catalog. Current onboarding is ad-hoc: manual catalog edits, one-off rollout scripts, and no standardized deprecation path. This leads to inconsistent version semantics, customer confusion when models are promoted/sunsetted, and manual rollback when quality regressions appear.

Scope:
- Onboard API-level changes and metadata schema for model entries (id, family, semver-like version, compatibility tags, quantization profile).
- Build CI checks that run a standardized evaluation suite (recall@10, MRR, embedding cosine density, embedding drift) and latency/throughput bench for candidate models.
- Implement canary/percent rollouts in the routing layer for embeddings endpoints with rule-based fallback to previous stable versions.
- Automate deprecation: schedule + customer notifications + retention of old model versions for a configurable window before hard-delete.
- Telemetry: add rollout-specific dashboards and alerts (quality regression, latency > threshold, increased error rate, abnormal embedding distribution shifts).

Non-goals: Model training and hyperparameter tuning. Full multi-tenant quota migration automation (we will provide flags and guidance, not forced migrations).

Design decisions to evaluate:
- Versioning: use family:v<major>.<minor> where major increments on breaking embedding geometry changes and minor increments on non-breaking improvements (e.g., quantization profile change).
- Rollout policy: start with linear percentage increases over 48 hours with quality checks at each step. Fail-open vs fail-closed policy negotiated with PM for each model.
- Storage retention: keep deprecated model artifacts and index for 90 days after deprecation unless customer opts out.

Outcomes: Reduced manual onboarding time, reproducible rollouts with automated safety gates, clearer model lifecycle for customers, dashboards for post-rollout analysis.
acceptance_criteria: Catalog schema updated and merged: model entry includes stable_id, semantic_version, compatibility_flags, quant_profile, signed_artifact_url
CI onboarding pipeline executes eval suite and emits pass/fail artifacts for a candidate model
Routing supports percent-based canary for embeddings endpoints with a fallback policy configured per model
Automated deprecation flow that creates a deprecation notice, notifies impacted customers, and enforces retention window before removal
Dashboards created: rollout-success-rate, embedding-latency-by-model, embedding-recall-trend; alerts for >5% recall drop or latency regressions above SLA
Rollback trigger implemented and tested (metric-based + manual) with end-to-end test that switches traffic back to stable version within 2 minutes
